passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel dietary supplement on blood pressure in adults aged 40–60. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 120 participants who were randomly assigned to either the supplement group (n = 60) or the placebo group (n = 60). Baseline systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) were recorded for all participants. After 12 weeks of daily supplementation, SBP and DBP were measured again. The study also collected data on heart rate (HR) and body mass index (BMI) to assess potential confounding variables. The researchers reported the following summary statistics in Table 1.
table_data:
Variable,Group A (Supplement),Group B (Placebo)
Baseline SBP (mmHg),132.4 ± 10.2,131.8 ± 9.9
Baseline DBP (mmHg),84.6 ± 5.7,85.1 ± 5.9
Week 12 SBP (mmHg),125.1 ± 9.8,129.3 ± 10.5
Week 12 DBP (mmHg),80.2 ± 5.4,83.7 ± 5.8
HR (bpm),72.3 ± 8.1,71.9 ± 8.3
BMI (kg/m^2),27.5 ± 2.3,27.7 ± 2.4
stem: Based on Table 1, which statement most accurately reflects the effect of the supplement on systolic blood pressure after 12 weeks?

options.A: The supplement group had a larger mean reduction in SBP than the placebo group.
options.B: Both groups showed similar reductions in SBP, indicating no effect of the supplement.
options.C: The placebo group had a greater reduction in SBP than the supplement group.
options.D: The supplement group’s SBP increased relative to baseline.

explanation: Correct: Supplement SBP fell 132.4 − 125.1 = 7.3 mmHg; placebo fell 131.8 − 129.3 = 2.5 mmHg, a 4.8 mmHg difference. Why the others are wrong: B) 7.3 versus 2.5 mmHg are not similar. C) The placebo reduction (2.5) was smaller than the supplement reduction (7.3). D) SBP fell from 132.4 to 125.1 mmHg in the supplement group.
trap: Assuming the placebo group’s smaller fall means no effect, or the reductions are similar; the difference is 4.8 mmHg.

stem: Which of the following design elements best supports attributing the observed SBP changes to the supplement?

options.A: Using a crossover design where participants receive both supplement and placebo.
options.B: Matching participants on baseline SBP before randomization.
options.C: Randomly assigning participants to supplement or placebo, balancing known and unknown confounders between groups.
options.D: Increasing the sample size to 200 participants.

explanation: Correct: Random assignment balances known and unknown confounders between groups, so differences can be attributed to the supplement. Why the others are wrong: A) A crossover design was not used and would add carry-over concerns. B) Matching on one variable does not balance other confounders and is not what makes the comparison causal. D) A larger sample improves precision but not confounding control.
trap: Choosing sample size or matching because they sound rigorous; neither balances unknown confounders the way random assignment does.

stem: Which statement is NOT supported by Table 1?

options.A: The supplement lowers SBP by 7.3 mmHg in every patient.
options.B: Mean week 12 DBP was lower in the supplement group than in the placebo group.
options.C: The two groups had similar mean baseline SBP.
options.D: Mean SBP in the placebo group fell by about 2.5 mmHg.

explanation: Correct: A) The 7.3 mmHg figure is a group mean; the table gives no individual responses. Why the others are wrong: B) 80.2 versus 83.7 mmHg; supported. C) 132.4 versus 131.8 mmHg; supported. D) 131.8 − 129.3 = 2.5 mmHg; supported.
trap: Reading the group mean change of 7.3 mmHg as the effect in every individual patient.

stem: Which conclusion is best supported by this trial?

options.A: The supplement should be prescribed to all hypertensive patients regardless of baseline BP.
options.B: Over 12 weeks in adults aged 40–60, the supplement lowered mean SBP about 4.8 mmHg more than placebo, but long‑term outcomes and other populations were not tested.
options.C: The supplement should be avoided because it raises heart rate.
options.D: The supplement should be used only for patients with BMI above 30 kg/m^2.

explanation: Correct: The SBP fall was 7.3 versus 2.5 mmHg (4.8 mmHg difference) in a 12-week trial of adults aged 40–60. Why the others are wrong: A) The trial did not enroll or analyze all hypertensive patients. C) Heart rate was similar (72.3 versus 71.9 bpm). D) Mean BMI was about 27.5 and no BMI subgroup was analyzed.
trap: Extending a short placebo-controlled result to all patients or to subgroups that were never analyzed.
